findings.issue: Reactions (add/remove) do not broadcast via Socket.io; frontend never receives real-time reaction updates
findings.impact: Users won't see reactions appear/ disappear in real time. Requires manual re-fetch or page reload, breaking the chat real-time experience. Frontend teams may add polling workarounds.
findings.fix: Emit reaction:added and reaction:removed events via Socket.io (getIO().to(channelRoom).emit(...)) in ReactionService.add and ReactionService.remove.

findings.issue: Channel mutations (create, update, delete, member add/remove) do not broadcast via Socket.io
findings.impact: Frontend won't see new channels, renamed channels, or member changes in real-time unless polling. Users remain in deleted channels. Sidebar doesn't update.
findings.fix: Emit channel:created, channel:updated, channel:deleted, channel:member_added, channel:member_removed events via Socket.io in ChannelService.

findings.issue: Dual response format: AppError.toJSON() returns { error: { code, message } } while failure() envelope returns { success: false, error: { code, message, status } } causing client contract confusion
findings.impact: Frontend code must handle two different error response shapes based on ?envelope=true query param that most clients never send. This creates fragile error handling and potential uncaught errors.
findings.fix: Standardize on a single error response format. Remove the ?envelope flag. Make error-handler always use the AppError.toJSON() format or always use the failure() format.

findings.issue: Inconsistent success response shapes: some endpoints return { success: true }, others return the resource directly, others return { message }, { messages }, { channel }, etc.
findings.impact: Frontend SDK and client code must handle multiple response shapes. Adding new endpoints requires checking which shape to use. Swagger/OpenAPI spec becomes inaccurate.
findings.fix: Adopt a single response envelope: either always wrap in { data: <resource> } or always return the resource directly. Audit all 21 route modules for consistency.

findings.issue: Idempotency only implemented for message creation; all other state-changing POST/PATCH/DELETE endpoints lack idempotency support
findings.impact: Network retries can cause duplicate channel creates, webhook creates, reaction adds, workspace creates, etc. No safe retry mechanism exists.
findings.fix: Implement idempotency middleware that checks Idempotency-Key header globally for all mutating endpoints. In-memory fallback is not suitable for multi-instance deployments.

findings.issue: Double-submit cookie CSRF uses timingSafeEqual with two user-controlled values, but the cookie token is stored without httpOnly flag, making it readable via JS
findings.impact: The CSRF cookie is accessible to JavaScript (httpOnly: false), weakening CSRF protection. An XSS vulnerability would give full access to CSRF tokens.
findings.fix: Set httpOnly: true on the CSRF cookie. Use a separate non-httpOnly cookie or header-based approach for the client-side token value.

findings.issue: Several route modules use inline validation (manual checks) instead of Zod schemas, bypassing the centralized validation layer
findings.impact: Inconsistent validation across endpoints. Missing schema documentation. Some endpoints accept raw input without type checking (e.g., sidebar routes, groups routes, livekit routes).
findings.fix: Create Zod schemas for all remaining endpoints (sidebar-categories, groups, scheduled-posts, consent, status, etc.) and use safeParse uniformly.

findings.issue: Thread join/leave/participants endpoints lack membership checks; any authenticated user can access any thread's participant list or join any thread
findings.impact: User could enumerate thread participants across the entire platform. Could join threads in channels they don't have access to.
findings.fix: Add requireChannelAccess middleware to thread endpoints (resolve channel from thread parent message).

findings.issue: User group routes lack workspace membership checks; any authenticated user can create/modify groups in any workspace
findings.impact: Authenticated user could create user groups in workspaces they don't belong to, or add/remove members from groups in any workspace.
findings.fix: Add requireWorkspaceMembership middleware to all group routes. Validate workspace ownership.

findings.issue: GET /workspaces/:workspaceId/channels and GET /channels/:id/members have no pagination, risking memory exhaustion on large workspaces
findings.impact: Workspace with thousands of channels or millions of members will cause out-of-memory errors or slow responses. No way to progressively load.
findings.fix: Add cursor-based or offset-based pagination to channel listing and member listing endpoints. Add default limit with max cap.

findings.issue: queryWithTimeout uses Promise.race which doesn't abort the underlying operation, causing resource leaks on timeout
findings.impact: When a query times out, the underlying Supabase fetch and database query continue executing. For long-running queries this wastes database connections and API server memory.
findings.fix: Pass AbortSignal to Supabase queries via the fetch implementation's Signal. Use AbortController to actually terminate in-flight requests on timeout.

findings.issue: Frontend has its own HTTP client (api.ts) that duplicates SDK logic, with different error handling, CSRF management, and response parsing than the @chat/sdk package
findings.impact: Two code paths for API calls that can diverge. SDK adds /v1 prefix automatically but api.ts also does. Error handling differs (SDK throws structured errors, api.ts throws plain Errors). OpenAPI spec may match neither.
findings.fix: Consolidate all API client usage into @chat/sdk. Remove duplicate api.ts or make it a thin wrapper around the SDK client.

findings.issue: OpenAPI spec loaded from static JSON file with no automated sync; likely out of date with actual routes and schemas
findings.impact: API consumers relying on OpenAPI spec will encounter undocumented endpoints, incorrect schemas, and wrong response shapes. Spec falls back to empty paths if file missing in production.
findings.fix: Generate OpenAPI spec dynamically from route registry and Zod schemas (e.g., using zod-to-openapi). Add CI check that verifies spec matches routes.

findings.issue: Error handler exposes stack traces in development mode via NODE_ENV check, but stack traces may contain file paths or internal structure
findings.impact: Internal file paths and code structure may leak in development environments. Minor info disclosure risk.
findings.fix: Use a configuration flag rather than NODE_ENV check for stack trace exposure. Never expose stack traces in error responses.

findings.issue: No API version negotiation or version pinning strategy beyond a single /v1 prefix; no sunset/deprecation headers
findings.impact: Breaking API changes cannot be rolled out gracefully. Consumers have no way to pin versions or get deprecation warnings.
findings.fix: Add Accept-Version header support or URL-based versioning (v2). Add Sunset and Deprecation response headers. Create a version migration guide.

findings.issue: Graceful shutdown destroys all sockets immediately without draining in-flight requests first
findings.impact: In-flight HTTP requests and WebSocket messages are terminated mid-processing. Users may see partial updates or failed message sends during deployment.
findings.fix: Add draining phase: stop accepting new requests, wait for active requests to complete (with timeout), then destroy idle sockets. Use httpServer.close() callback properly.

findings.issue: Basic health endpoint (GET /) returns hardcoded status without checking database or Redis connectivity
findings.impact: Health check passes even when database is unreachable. Load balancer/ orchestrator won't detect degraded state.
findings.fix: Remove basic health endpoint or add dependency health checks. Use getFullHealth() as the primary health endpoint. Add Redis ping check.

findings.issue: Webhook create schema allows optional secret field but stores it in plaintext in the database
findings.impact: Webhook secrets are stored as plaintext in the webhook_endpoints table. Database compromise would expose all webhook signing secrets.
findings.fix: Hash webhook secrets at rest using a KDF (e.g., bcrypt/argon2). Only return masked versions in API responses.

findings.issue: Socket.io client library installed but frontend has no app-level socket lifecycle management; socket only initialized lazily in use-presence hook
findings.impact: Real-time features like typing indicators, new message notifications, and channel updates don't work via Socket.io. The library exists but is effectively dead code for the main chat experience.
findings.fix: Create a SocketProvider context that initializes the socket at app root. Connect socket lifecycle to auth state (connect on login, disconnect on logout).

findings.issue: test job runs before build via turbo dependency chain (turbo test depends on build), but the test job in validate.yml runs before the build job without building first
findings.impact: pnpm test may fail in CI because it depends on build artifacts that don't exist yet. The test step runs in parallel with build rather than sequentially.
findings.fix: Add a build step before pnpm test, or configure turbo.json test task to not depend on build, or restructure validate.yml jobs in proper dependency order.

findings.issue: diff-coverage job uses pnpm test -- --changed --coverage but the --changed flag runs tests for changed files only; coverage thresholds apply to total project, not diff
findings.impact: False sense of coverage compliance: 40% line coverage on the entire project does not protect against untested new code in a PR.
findings.fix: Replace with a proper diff-coverage tool (e.g., istanbul ignore patterns) that checks coverage on only the lines changed in the PR. Consider using codecov or coveralls.

findings.issue: Supabase anon key hardcoded as fallback in workflow YAML: 'NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY: ${{ secrets.SUPABASE_ANON_KEY || 'eyJ...' }}'
findings.impact: The plaintext fallback key is visible to anyone with read access to the repo. Exposes anon key in CI logs and YAML.
findings.fix: Remove hardcoded fallback. Fail CI if SUPABASE_ANON_KEY secret is not set.

findings.issue: Database migrations run before the droplet SSH setup; if supabase link fails, migration runs but droplet may not exist yet
findings.impact: Race condition: migrations could fail on non-existent project while deploy proceeds, or migrations succeed but deploy fails, leaving state inconsistent.
findings.fix: Move database migrations after droplet setup, or add supabase link verification before migration.

findings.issue: Redundant workflows: hardening.yml and hardening-automation-runner.yml both run the same hardening pipeline. governance.yml and platform.yml both call run_full.ps1.
findings.impact: Workflow sprawl (20 files) increases maintenance burden. Operators unsure which workflow to trigger.
findings.fix: Consolidate: keep hardening-automation-runner.yml, remove hardening.yml. Consolidate governance and platform into one.

findings.issue: audit-badges-autocommit and audit-ci-autocommit both auto-commit changes on push to develop/main, potentially causing commit loops with CI re-triggers
findings.impact: Auto-commits trigger new CI runs, creating cascading pipeline executions. Wastes compute and pollutes git history.
findings.fix: Use [skip ci] in auto-commit messages, or reduce scope to workflow_dispatch only. Add path filters to avoid triggering deploy on badge changes.

findings.issue: branch-protection check runs on every PR from any actor, but the check doesn't enforce anything — it only reports
findings.impact: Informational only; no actual enforcement of branch protection rules. Provides false confidence in CI output.
findings.fix: Either enforce by failing the job on missing protection, or remove the job and rely on GitHub's native branch protection settings.

findings.issue: Deploy workflow writes secrets to .env file via inline shell script in SSH — secrets appear in plaintext in workflow run logs if script execution is verbose
findings.impact: Potential secret leakage in CI logs. Secrets are interpolated by GitHub Actions before SSH execution.
findings.fix: Use environment files (.env) passed as GitHub Actions env context, or use the droplet's secrets manager. Set set -x only where needed.

findings.issue: Each job re-installs dependencies independently (pnpm install per lint, typecheck, test, build, e2e) — no caching across jobs
findings.impact: CI pipeline takes 5-8 minutes per job for dependency install on cache miss. 5+ jobs = 25-40 minutes total.
findings.fix: Use pnpm workspace-level caching with GitHub Actions cache action to share node_modules across jobs. Or use a single job for all checks.

findings.issue: Majority of E2E test scenarios are skipped (test.skip) due to missing Supabase test project
findings.impact: Critical user journeys (auth, workspace, channels, messaging, WebSocket, notifications, webhooks, search) cannot be verified end-to-end. 27 of 35 test cases skipped.
findings.fix: Provision a Supabase test project or implement local Supabase mock with seeded test data for CI pipeline. Unskip all flow tests.

findings.issue: CI E2E job has no Supabase local instance; PLAYWRIGHT_BASE_URL points to Next.js dev server that cannot authenticate without Supabase
findings.impact: E2E tests will fail in CI because auth flows depend on Supabase. The webServer block starts Next.js but Supabase local stack is never started.
findings.fix: Add supabase start step before E2E job, or configure test-specific Supabase project with seeded data and use supabase db reset.

findings.issue: Only Chromium browser configured; no Firefox/WebKit coverage
findings.impact: Browser-specific rendering and API differences go undetected. Affects ~10% of users on Firefox/Safari.
findings.fix: Add Firefox and WebKit projects to playwright.config.ts with appropriate viewport presets.

findings.issue: E2E messaging tests depend on test data created by prior tests (workspace/channel must exist), making tests order-dependent and fragile
findings.impact: Tests fail when run in isolation or in parallel; CI flakiness on partial re-runs.
findings.fix: Use beforeAll hooks or fixtures to create required workspace/channel independently per test file, or use Playwright project dependencies.

findings.issue: k6 load test only hits /healthz endpoint; no chat send, socket, search, or notification scenarios
findings.impact: Load testing provides no meaningful capacity or bottleneck data for core chat flows.
findings.fix: Add k6 scenarios for: concurrent message sends, WebSocket connect storm, search under load, notification fanout to N users.

findings.issue: Visual snapshots cover only login, settings, and 404 pages; no chat view, channel list, sidebar, dark mode, or mobile states
findings.impact: High-risk visual regressions in core chat UI go undetected. No dark mode or responsive coverage.
findings.fix: Add snapshots for: channel view (empty/populated), sidebar collapsed/expanded, dark mode toggle, mobile nav, long message overflow, emoji picker, dialogs.

findings.issue: Coverage thresholds set low (lines: 40, functions: 30, branches: 30, statements: 40)
findings.impact: Low thresholds allow significant untested code to pass CI without warning.
findings.fix: Raise thresholds incrementally: lines 60, functions 50, branches 50, statements 60.

findings.issue: CI k6 workflow only runs smoke test (10 VUs, 30s) with no load test execution
findings.impact: Weekly load test cron runs smoke test, not the actual load test. No ramp-up or capacity verification.
findings.fix: Add a load-test job that runs tests/k6/load-test.js with production-like ramp profile. Keep smoke test as quick sanity.

findings.issue: No test data fixtures or seed scripts; E2E tests hardcode test email and workspace names
findings.impact: Tests are brittle and hard to reproduce across environments without consistent test data setup.
findings.fix: Create test data fixtures (JSON/TS) with mock workspace, channel, user, and message data. Use Playwright test fixtures to inject.

findings.issue: Production deployment workflow lacks mandatory manual approval step before deployment to production
findings.impact: Any push to main or manual trigger deploys to production without human oversight. A malicious or buggy commit reaches users with no opportunity for review or rollback decision.
findings.fix: Add an 'environment: production' deployment protection rule with required reviewers in GitHub. Add a 'wait-for-approval' step before the deploy job that blocks until an authorized user approves.

findings.issue: CI/CD uses `:latest` image tags which overwrite previous production images, preventing rapid rollback to a known-good version
findings.impact: If a broken deployment is promoted to production, rolling back requires rebuilding the old image instead of redeploying a tagged version. The previous `:latest` image is lost.
findings.fix: Tag production images with both `:latest` and a specific SHA-based tag (e.g., `:git-sha-${GITHUB_SHA}`). Add a rollback workflow that accepts a SHA tag and deploys that version.

findings.issue: Production Docker Compose uses Caddy for TLS while development uses raw ports — no parity on reverse proxy configuration
findings.impact: CORS, cookie security settings, and CSP headers behave differently between environments. A bug in Caddy config only manifests in production, and production TLS issues cannot be reproduced locally.
findings.fix: Add a local Caddyfile.dev for development that mirrors production Caddy configuration but with self-signed certs. Add a docker-compose.override.yml for local TLS testing.

findings.issue: Development deployment to DigitalOcean uses same Docker Compose as production with only minor env var differences
findings.impact: A breaking change in Docker Compose that only manifests on the remote environment cannot be detected before promoting to production. Dev and prod should run independently as isolated stacks.
findings.fix: Use separate Docker Compose project names (--project-name) to isolate stacks. Add environment prefix to container names. Ensure dev and prod can coexist on the same host without conflict.

findings.issue: No smoke test or health check validation step after production deployment completes
findings.impact: A deployment that starts but immediately fails health checks goes undetected by CI/CD. Operators only learn about failures through user reports.
findings.fix: Add a post-deploy smoke test step that: (1) hits the /health endpoint, (2) verifies 200 response, (3) checks database connectivity, (4) sends a test WebSocket message. Rollback automatically if smoke tests fail.

findings.issue: Terraform IaC only provisions a single droplet shared between dev and prod environments
findings.impact: Development and production share the same compute resources. A load test or memory leak in dev can impact production performance and vice versa.
findings.fix: Separate Terraform workspaces for dev and prod with isolated droplets. Add environment variable to Terraform to select target. Increase resource allocation for prod.

findings.issue: Workspace membership middleware uses 'deny' permission check but does not verify workspace-level role for granular permission enforcement
findings.impact: A member can be denied membership without checking if they have the specific permission needed for an operation, potentially allowing unauthorized actions within a workspace they are a member of.
findings.fix: Add requirePermission() middleware after requireMembership() on all workspace-scoped endpoints to verify both membership AND the specific permission required.

findings.issue: Policy structure is flat with no distinction between dev, RC, production, and hotfix release tiers
findings.impact: All releases are subject to the same policy thresholds, making it impossible to grant temporary exceptions for hotfixes or allow faster iteration in dev branches.
findings.fix: Implement tiered policy files: governance.dev.json, governance.rc.json, governance.prod.json, governance.hotfix.json. Each tier inherits from the base but can override thresholds with explicit approval gates.

findings.issue: No hotfix exception procedure defined; hotfixes would either be blocked by standard gates or bypass them without compensating controls
findings.impact: During a production incident requiring a rapid fix, operators have no documented procedure for granting policy exceptions with mandatory post-incident review.
findings.fix: Add a 'hotfix' policy tier that relaxes gating thresholds but requires: (1) documented severity justification, (2) at least one peer review, (3) post-deploy audit within 24h, (4) mandatory follow-up to re-apply standard gates.

findings.issue: Audit logging uses in-memory retry queue that can lose entries and has no mechanism to detect missed audit events
findings.impact: A restart during audit log processing can silently lose audit entries for sensitive actions (permission changes, workspace deletion), breaking the audit chain.
findings.fix: Add a database audit_log_retry table for persistent queuing. Implement a periodic reconciliation job that detects gaps in audit log sequences. Add an alert for audit logging failures.

findings.issue: CI/CD audit gates use a single threshold regardless of branch (develop vs main vs hotfix)
findings.impact: A PR with P2 findings to develop is blocked with the same severity as a production release, slowing iteration velocity without proportional risk assessment.
findings.fix: Map CI/CD gates to policy tiers: PRs to develop allow P2/P3 with warnings, PRs to main/staging block P1+, hotfix releases allow P1 with documented exceptions.

findings.issue: Policy file lacks versioning or change history; modifications to thresholds are not auditable
findings.impact: Policy drift is undetectable. There is no record of when or why thresholds were changed, making governance reviews difficult.
findings.fix: Add a version field to policy JSON files. Enforce that policy changes go through a PR with audit trail. Consider storing policy versions alongside run artifacts.

findings.issue: Permission 'workspace:delete' granted to admin role but workspace deletion should require owner-only
findings.impact: A workspace admin can delete a workspace, potentially causing data loss without owner consent. Admins have the same destructive permissions as owners.
findings.fix: Remove 'workspace:delete' from the admin role permissions list. Only 'owner' should have workspace deletion capability.

findings.issue: BullMQ queues require Redis and have no fallback when Redis is unavailable
findings.impact: If Redis goes down, all queue-dependent workers (webhook delivery, notifications, search indexing, cleanup, data retention) stop functioning entirely. No jobs can be enqueued or processed.
findings.fix: Implement a Redis connection fallback strategy: use in-memory queue with periodic flush when Redis is available, or add a 'paused' mode that stores jobs in the database for later processing.

findings.issue: No bulkhead or isolation pattern between different queue processors sharing the same Redis connection
findings.impact: A single misbehaving queue processor (e.g., blocked webhook delivery) can exhaust the Redis connection pool and starve other processors (notifications, search indexing).
findings.fix: Use separate Redis connection pools per queue processor, or configure max concurrency per processor independently. Monitor Redis connection usage per processor.

findings.issue: Circuit breaker metrics are tracked but not exposed via the /metrics endpoint for monitoring
findings.impact: Operators cannot monitor circuit breaker state (open/closed/half-open) in dashboards or alert on cascading circuit breaker failures.
findings.fix: Integrate circuit breaker stats into the Prometheus metrics endpoint. Expose breaker status, failure rate, and request volume as gauges.

findings.issue: No database connection pool health monitoring; Supabase client retries internally but application has no visibility into pool exhaustion
findings.impact: If Supabase connection pool is exhausted, requests silently hang until timeout with no operator visibility into the pool utilization.
findings.fix: Add a database pool health gauge metric. Implement a connection pool timeout alert. Consider adding a readiness check that verifies database connection pool availability.

findings.issue: In-memory idempotency fallback limited to single process — resets on restart, not shared across instances
findings.impact: In a multi-instance deployment, idempotency keys stored in-memory on one instance are invisible to another. A restart loses all idempotency state, potentially allowing duplicate message processing.
findings.fix: Add a database-backed idempotency store as a secondary fallback. Document that in-memory fallback is single-instance-only and provide a migration path to Redis.

findings.issue: Chaos engineering prompt exists but no actual chaos tests are executed or integrated into CI/CD
findings.impact: Resilience characteristics (circuit breaker behavior, graceful degradation, fallback paths) are untested. Failures in production may behave differently than expected.
findings.fix: Implement chaos testing scenarios: Redis failure, database latency injection, queue worker crash, and API service restart. Add a scheduled chaos test workflow.

findings.issue: Webhook delivery uses randomUUID as idempotency key instead of deterministic hash of payload
findings.impact: Random idempotency keys do not prevent duplicate deliveries for identical payloads because each retry generates a new key.
findings.fix: Generate idempotency key as SHA-256 hash of (event + payload + webhookId) to ensure identical payloads produce identical keys. Use the delivery.id for tracking.

findings.issue: Audit log retry queue is purely in-memory with no persistence — lost on process restart
findings.impact: If the API process restarts while audit entries are queued for retry, those entries are lost permanently with no record.
findings.fix: Persist failed audit entries to a database table (audit_log_retry_queue) or use BullMQ for the audit queue. Add a startup recovery job that retries unprocessed entries.

findings.issue: Docker images pushed to GHCR are not signed/attested; no cosign, notation, or SLSA provenance
findings.impact: No cryptographic verification that images were built from trusted CI. Compromised CI could inject malicious images without detection at deploy time.
findings.fix: Integrate cosign for image signing + keyless signing via GitHub OIDC. Add SLSA generator workflow for provenance attestation.

findings.issue: No multi-stage build verification; package installation may include dev dependencies in production image if not properly staged
findings.impact: Production images may contain unnecessary binaries and packages, increasing attack surface and image size.
findings.fix: Audit Dockerfiles to confirm multi-stage build separation. Add .dockerignore entry for dev dependencies. Run `docker scout` or `trivy` on final stage only.

findings.issue: No automated license compliance check; open-source dependency licenses are not reviewed or tracked
findings.impact: Risk of GPL/AGPL viral license contamination or incompatible license terms in production distribution.
findings.fix: Add pnpm-licenses or license-checker to CI. Fail build on prohibited licenses (AGPL, non-commercial). Add license report to SBOM.

findings.issue: Trivy fs scan runs on every PR but vulnerability database is not updated; stale DB misses recent CVEs
findings.impact: Scans may miss vulnerabilities discovered between cached DB updates. False sense of security.
findings.fix: Add trivy DB update step before scanning: `trivy image --download-db-only` or use `--cache-dir` with scheduled refresh.

findings.issue: Trivy image scan runs with continue-on-error: true, so vulnerabilities do not block the build
findings.impact: HIGH/CRITICAL vulnerabilities in Docker images are reported but do not prevent deployment. No enforcement.
findings.fix: Set continue-on-error: false for production builds, or add a post-scan step that fails if CRITICAL vulnerabilities exceed threshold (e.g., > 0).

findings.issue: SBOM generation only runs on push to develop, not on main/release builds
findings.impact: Production releases lack SBOM artifacts for vulnerability tracking and compliance.
findings.fix: Enable SBOM generation for all pushes to main/release branches. Upload SBOM as release asset.

findings.issue: Dependabot batch groups (minor-patch) may cause delayed patch updates for critical security fixes
findings.impact: Critical security patches bundled with non-urgent changes may be delayed by cooldown period (15 days).
findings.fix: Exempt 'security' update type from batch grouping so critical patches are opened immediately. Add `ignored_updates` only for non-security.
